commit_message:
Optimize SET/INCR*/DECR*/SETRANGE/APPEND by reducing duplicate computation (#13505)

- Avoid addReplyLongLong (which converts back to string) the value we
already have as a robj, by using addReplyProto + addReply
- Avoid doing dbFind Twice for the same dictEntry on
INCR*/DECR*/SETRANGE/APPEND commands.
- Avoid multiple sdslen calls with the same input on setrangeCommand and
appendCommand
- Introduce setKeyWithDictEntry, which is like setKey(), but accepts an
optional dictEntry input: Avoids the second dictFind in SET command

---------

Co-authored-by: debing.sun <debing.sun@redis.com>

fix_commit_message:
avoid possible use-after-free with module KSN changes (#13875)

in #13505, we changed the code to use the string value of the key rather
than the integer value on the stack, but we have a test in
unit/moduleapi/keyspace_events that uses keyspace notification hook to
modify the value with RM_StringDMA, which can cause this value to be
released before used. the reason it didn't happen so far is because we
were using shared integers, so releasing the object doesn't free it.
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 2a189709e098 on top of intro 05aed4cab976 via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (UseAfterFree): incrDecrCommand() (backing INCR/DECR/INCRBY/DECRBY) replies to the client by reading data out of the 'new' robj representing the key's new string value, via addReplyLongLongFromStr(c,new). This call happens after notifyKeyspaceEvent(), which can synchronously run a loaded module's keyspace-notification callback. If that callback calls RM_StringDMA (direct memory access) on the same key, it can trigger reallocation/release of the underlying sds buffer backing 'new', so the later addReplyLongLongFromStr reads freed/stale memory -- a classic use-after-free. Root cause: PR #13505 optimized INCR/DECR (and related commands) to avoid re-serializing the integer to a string for the reply, by replying directly from the heap-allocated robj ('new') that was just stored into the keyspace, rather than from a stack-local integer copy. However the reply-generation call was left positioned after signalModifiedKey()/notifyKeyspaceEvent(), which can re-enter into module keyspace-notification subscriber callbacks. Those callbacks run with full API access (including RM_StringDMA) to the key that now holds 'new', so they can free/reallocate the buffer 'new' points to before the deferred reply call reads it. Previously, replies used a stack copy of the integer value (or values were small/shared integer objects that aren't actually freed by dict replacement), so no live reference into freed heap memory was retained across the notification call.
